title: How much wrapping paper do I need for a rectangular gift box?
summary: Allow about 2 inches of overlap at the seam and leave paper extending about two-thirds of the box height beyond each end.

items.title: How much wrapping paper do I need for a rectangular gift box?
items.summary: Cut a sheet that goes once around the box with about 2 inches to spare at the seam. For a box 12 inches long, 8 inches wide and 3 inches high, a 24 × 16-inch sheet works for a straight wrap. The 24-inch edge covers the width twice (16 inches), the height twice (6 inches) and a 2-inch overlap. The 16-inch edge runs along the 12-inch length, leaving 2 inches to fold at each end.
items.buyerNote: Lay the closed box on the back of the paper with its lid facing down. Before cutting, pull the paper around the box to check the seam overlap. At each open end, lift the paper against the end panel. It should reach roughly two-thirds of the way up. Center the box so both ends have the same allowance.
